one_liner: Estimates each number's own chance of being drawn from earlier draws, each older draw counting 149/150 as much as the next (about two years' half-life), starting from the fair-draw chance.
registry_status_reason: Released by package REL-1 (releases and WF-1 design v0.1r1, owner decisions WF1-1 and WF1-2, ratified 31 October 2026). Contract runs on real data need the separate real-development gate.
short_explanation: E_6 treats each number on its own. For every earlier draw it notes whether the number was drawn, and estimates the number's chance with the standard Beta-Bernoulli model: it starts from the fair-draw chance (7 in 35 for a main number, 1 in 20 for the Powerball), worth one draw of evidence, and updates it with the history. Older draws count for less: each draw back counts 149/150 as much as the one after it, so a draw about 104 draws (two years of weekly draws) old counts half as much as the newest. This down-weighting makes it a discounted update, not the plain Bayesian posterior. The estimated chances are the scores: its top pick is the highest-ranked numbers and its inverse pick the lowest-ranked, with exact ties settled by the project tie rule (TIE_SHA256_V1). The chances are also published as probabilities, labelled as uncalibrated model outputs, because the model ignores that the main numbers are drawn together. It uses only which numbers were drawn, not their order or the dates. If the draws are fair, it is not expected to beat chance.
